newsitem.title: FRANCE: French train strike eases, Monday seen near normal.
newsitem.headline: French train strike eases, Monday seen near normal.

text.p: A strike by French train conductors disrupted rail traffic for a fifth day on Sunday, prolonging travellers' misery over a long holiday weekend.

The state railway company SNCF cancelled one in three trains on most of its main lines, but said traffic would be near normal on Monday, when holidaymakers return from the three-day Pentecost weekend, as conductors in 15 out of 24 regions had voted to resume work.
The stoppage did not affect high-speed Eurostar trains to London through the Channel Tunnel.
Most high-speed and all other main lines would return to normal on Monday, except that about one train in three would be cancelled between Paris and Lille, Bordeaux, Toulouse, the SNCF said.
Despite talk of a breakthrough last Friday, the strike dragged on into the Pentecost weekend after most conductors voted to reject concessions won by unions in negotiations with the SNCF.
In a rift between unions, the hardline Sud-Rail, kept out of talks because it represents a minority of staff, said the concessions fell far short of its demands.
The Socialist-backed CFDT union, France's largest, said it had won significant concesssions and urged its members to examine the whole package on offer when voting on their next move.
The SNCF apologised to its travellers and said the strike would badly hurt the company.
The conductors staged a similar strike last month in another sign of opposition to the austerity policies of the centre-right government of Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
